<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Students at Arlington Secondary School were polled regarding their favourite drinks.

![papers/aldenham-school/2019/sample-paper-1/s01-q23-i00.png](/assets/papers/aldenham-school/2019/sample-paper-1/s01-q23-i00.png "papers/aldenham-school/2019/sample-paper-1/s01-q23-i00.png")

Given that there are $600$ students at the school, how many more preferred root beer than lemonade?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Students at Arlington Secondary School were polled regarding their favourite drinks.
<emptyline>
%image%
<emptyline>
Given that there are $600$ students at the school, how many more preferred root beer than lemonade?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Difference}                       &= \dfrac {1}{4} \times 600 - \dfrac {1}{6} \times 600 \\\\
                                        &= (\dfrac {1}{4} - \dfrac {1}{6}) \times 600 \\\\
                                        &= (\dfrac {1 \times 3}{4 \times 3} - \dfrac {1 \times 2}{6 \times 2} ) \times 600 \\\\
                                        &= (\dfrac {3}{12} - \dfrac {2}{12} ) \times 600 \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {1}{12}  \times 600 \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {12 \times 50}{12} \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {\cancel{12} \times 50}{\cancel{12}} \\\\
                                        &= 50
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$50$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

The number of boys who fail the test is $15$.

How many boys pass the test?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">The number of boys who fail the test is $15$.
<emptyline>
How many boys pass the test?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the total number of boys $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {3} {12} \times a            &= 15 \\\\
a                                   &= \dfrac {15 \times 12} {3} \\\\
a                                   &= \dfrac {3 \times 5 \times 12} {3} \\\\
a                                   &= \dfrac {\cancel {3} \times 5 \times 12} {\cancel {3}} \\\\
a                                   &= 5 \times 12 \\\\
a                                   &= 60
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Students who passed}  &= a - 15 \\\\
                            &= 60 - 15 \\\\
                            &= 45
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$45$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Students in $6\text{C}$ were asked about their favourite sports. The results are displayed in the pie chart below.

![papers/aldenham-school/sample/sample-paper-3/s01-q21-i00.png](/assets/papers/aldenham-school/sample/sample-paper-3/s01-q21-i00.png "papers/aldenham-school/sample/sample-paper-3/s01-q21-i00.png")

$36$ students chose hockey.

How many students chose swimming?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Students in $6\text{C}$ were asked about their favourite sports. The results are displayed in the pie chart below.
<emptyline>
%image%
<emptyline>
$36$ students chose hockey.
<emptyline>
How many students chose swimming?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the total number of students in 6C $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac{60}{360} \times a        &= 36 \\\\
a                               &= \dfrac{36 \times 360}{60} \\\\
a                               &= \dfrac{36 \times 60 \times 6}{60} \\\\
a                               &= \dfrac{36 \times \cancel{60} \times 6}{\cancel{60}} \\\\
a                               &= 36 \times 6 \\\\
a                               &= 216
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Students who chose swimming}  &= \dfrac{90}{360} \times a \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac{90}{360} \times 216 \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac{90 \times 216}{360}  \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac{90 \times 4 \times 54}{90 \times 4}  \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac{\cancel{90}  \times \cancel{4} \times 54}{\cancel{90} \times \cancel{4}} \\\\
                                    &= 54
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$54$

</div>
</div>

</div>

a                               &= 36 \times 6 \\\\

\end{aligned}
$
<emptyline>

                                    &= \dfrac{90}{360} \times 216 \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac{90 \times 216}{360}  \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac{90 \times 4 \times 54}{90 \times 4}  \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac{\cancel{90}  \times \cancel{4} \times 54}{\cancel{90} \times \cancel{4}} \\\\

$

<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the total number of people $= a$

As per the graph,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {30} {360} \times a          &= 5 \\\\
a                                   &= \dfrac {5 \times 360} {30} \\\\
a                                   &= \dfrac {5 \times 12 \times 30} {30} \\\\
a                                   &= \dfrac {5 \times 12 \times \cancel {30}} {\cancel {30}} \\\\
a                                   &= 5 \times 12 \\\\
a                                   &= 60
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {People who own silver car}   &= \dfrac {180} {360} \times a \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {180} {360} \times 60 \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {180 \times 60} {360} \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {180 \times 2 \times 30} {2 \times 180} \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {\cancel {180} \times \cancel {2} \times 30} {\cancel {2} \times \cancel {180}} \\\\
                                    &= 30
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$30$

</div>

![papers/alderley-edge-school-for-girls/2019/sample-paper-1/s02-q17-s04-i00.png](/assets/papers/alderley-edge-school-for-girls/2019/sample-paper-1/s02-q17-s04-i00.png "papers/alderley-edge-school-for-girls/2019/sample-paper-1/s02-q17-s04-i00.png")

Do I have enough tiles to make the next square, of side length $4?$
Show working to explain your answer.

\end{aligned}

$

**Working**

Let the total number of students $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {120} {360} \times a     &= 20 \\\\
a                               &= \dfrac {20 \times 360} {120} \\\\
a                               &= \dfrac {20 \times 3 \times 120} {120} \\\\
a                               &= \dfrac {20 \times 3 \times \cancel {120}} {\cancel {120}} \\\\
a                               &= 20 \times 3 \\\\
a                               &= 60
\end{aligned}
$

Total number of students $= 60$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Seven out of forty pupils said they watch the news on television. 
What angle would this be on a pie chart? 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Seven out of forty pupils said they watch the news on television. 
What angle would this be on a pie chart? 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Angle}   &= \dfrac {7} {40} \times 360 \\\\
                &= \dfrac {7 \times 360} {40} \\\\
                &= \dfrac {7 \times 9 \times 40} {40} \\\\
                &= \dfrac {7 \times 9 \times \cancel {40}} {\cancel {40}} \\\\
                &= 7 \times 9 \\\\
                &= 63 \degree
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$63 \degree$

</div>

<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

</code></pre>

<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Side of the square}       &= \sqrt {(0 - 4) ^ 2 + (4 - 1) ^ 2} \\\\
                                &= \sqrt {(-4) ^ 2 + 3 ^ 2} \\\\
                                &= \sqrt {16 + 9} \\\\
                                &= \sqrt {25} \\\\
                                &= 5 \\\\
\text{Area of the square}       &= \text{(Side of the square)} ^ 2 \\\\
                                &= 5 ^ 2 \\\\
                                &= 25
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

What is the area of the triangle formed by these three points?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">What is the area of the triangle formed by these three points?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Base of the triangle}     &= \sqrt {(-1 - 2) ^ 2 + (1 - 1) ^ 2} \\\\
                                &= \sqrt {(-3) ^ 2 + 0 ^ 2} \\\\
                                &= \sqrt {9 + 0} \\\\
                                &= \sqrt {9} \\\\
                                &= 3 \\\\
\text{Height of the triangle}   &= 2 - 1 \\\\
                                &= 1 \\\\
\text{Area of the square}       &= \dfrac {1} {2} \times \text{(Base of the triangle)} \times \text{(Height of the triangle)} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {1} {2} \times 3 \times 1 \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {3} {2} \\\\
                                &= 1.5
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$1.5$

**Question**

What fraction of the patients seen by Dr Patel in July were children?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">What fraction of the patients seen by Dr Patel in July were children?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Fraction}    &= \dfrac {240 - 80} {240} \\\\
                    &= \dfrac {160} {240} \\\\
                    &= \dfrac {2 \times 80} {3 \times 80} \\\\
                    &= \dfrac {2 \times \cancel {80}} {3 \times \cancel {80}} \\\\
                    &= \dfrac {2} {3}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

**Question**

A square of side length $3 \ \text{cm}$ is divided into three
rectangles of equal size.

The middle rectangle is removed and replaced on the side of the 
original square to form an octagon as shown.

How many times bigger is the perimeter of the octagon than 
the perimeter of the original square?

![papers/bancrofts-school/2021/sample-paper-7/s01-q35-s02-i00.png](/assets/papers/bancrofts-school/2021/sample-paper-7/s01-q35-s02-i00.png "papers/bancrofts-school/2021/sample-paper-7/s01-q35-s02-i00.png")

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">A square of side length $3 \ \text{cm}$ is divided into three
rectangles of equal size.

<emptyline>
%image%
</code></pre>
</div>

                                &= 20 \ \text{cm} \\\\

                                &= 8 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$

<div class="question_envelope rag_not_found subquestion">
<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

This formula tells you how tall a boy is likely to be when he grows up.

| Add the mother's and father's heights. Divide by $2$. Add $7 \ \text{cm}$ to the result. The boy is likely to be this height, plus or minus $10 \ \text{cm}$. |
|:-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------:|

Marc's mother is $168\ \text{cm}$ tall. His father is $194\ \text{cm}$ tall.

What is the greatest height Marc is likely to be when he grows up? 

Show your working.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">This formula tells you how tall a boy is likely to be when he grows up.
<emptyline>
| Add the mother's and father's heights. Divide by $2$. Add $7 \ \text{cm}$ to the result. The boy is likely to be this height, plus or minus $10 \ \text{cm}$. |
|:-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------:|
<emptyline>
Marc's mother is $168\ \text{cm}$ tall. His father is $194\ \text{cm}$ tall.
<emptyline>
What is the greatest height Marc is likely to be when he grows up? 
<emptyline>
Show your working.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Max height of Marc}           &= \dfrac {1} {2} \times (168 + 194) + 7 + 10 \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {168 + 194} {2} + 17  \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {362} {2} + 17 \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {2 \times 181} {2} + 17 \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {\cancel 2 \times 181} {\cancel 2} + 17 \\\\
                                    &= 181 + 17 \\\\
                                    &= 198 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$191 \ \text{cm}$

</div>

<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

What is the area of the rectangle?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">What is the area of the rectangle?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Length of rectangle}      &= \sqrt {(4 - 4) ^ 2 + (5 - 1) ^ 2} \\\\
                                &= \sqrt {0 ^ 2 + 4 ^ 2} \\\\
                                &= \sqrt {0 + 16} \\\\
                                &= \sqrt {16} \\\\
                                &= 4 \ \text{cm} \\\\
\text{Breadth of rectangle}     &= \sqrt {(-1 - 4) ^ 2 + (1 - 1) ^ 2} \\\\
                                &= \sqrt {(-5)) ^ 2 + 0 ^ 2} \\\\
                                &= \sqrt {25 + 0} \\\\
                                &= \sqrt {25} \\\\
                                &= 5 \ \text{cm} \\\\
\text{Area of rectangle}        &= \text{Length of rectangle} \times \text{Breadth of rectangle} \\\\
                                &= 4 \times 5 \\\\
                                &= 20 \ {\text{cm}} ^ 2
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$20$

</div>
</div>

\text {Total cousins} &= 3 \times 0 + 6 \times 1 + 8 \times 2 + 5 \times 3 + 3 \times 4 \\\\
                      &= 0 + 6 + 16 + 15 + 12 \\\\
                      &= 49
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

Show the coordinates of the origin and distance $2, 5, 6$ and $y$


*ABBR: TODO:: Add drawing ends.*


Using equivalent ratio,

$
\begin{aligned}
2 : 5                                           &= 6 : y \\\\
\dfrac {2} {5}                                  &= \dfrac {6} {y} \\\\
2 \times y                                      &= 6 \times 5 \\\\
y                                               &= \dfrac {6 \times 5} {2} \\\\
y                                               &= \dfrac {2 \times 3 \times 5} {2} \\\\
y                                               &= \dfrac {\cancel 2 \times 3 \times 5} {\cancel 2} \\\\
y                                               &= 3 \times 5 \\\\
y                                               &= 15
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

| Red | Blue | Green | Yellow | Orange |
|:---:|:----:|:-----:|:------:|:------:|
| $5$ |  $7$ |  $8$  |   $3$  |   $2$  |

A pie chart is drawn to show children's favourite colour using the table above. What size angle would represent Red?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">| Red | Blue | Green | Yellow | Orange |
|:---:|:----:|:-----:|:------:|:------:|
| $5$ |  $7$ |  $8$  |   $3$  |   $2$  |
<emptyline>
A pie chart is drawn to show children's favourite colour using the table above. What size angle would represent Red?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Angle red}                            &= \dfrac {5} {5 + 7 + 8 + 3 + 2} \times 360 \\\\
                                            &= \dfrac {5} {25} \times 360 \\\\
                                            &= \dfrac {5 \times 360} {25} \\\\
                                            &= \dfrac {5 \times 5 \times 72} {5 \times 5} \\\\
                                            &= \dfrac {\cancel 5 \times \cancel 5 \times 72} {\cancel 5 \times \cancel 5} \\\\
                                            &= 72 \degree
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$72 \degree$

$180$ children were surveyed as to their favourite pastime. The results are in the pie chart above. How many children prefer computers?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

                                                        &= \dfrac {93 \times \cancel{2} \times \cancel{180}} {\cancel{2} \times \cancel{180}} \\\\
                                                        &= 93
\end{aligned}
$

$40$ students were asked which was their favourite colour. How many students chose Yellow?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">%image%
<emptyline>
$40$ students were asked which was their favourite colour. How many students chose Yellow?
</code></pre>

<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Students who choose yellow}               &= \dfrac {45} {360} \times 40 \\\\
                                                &= \dfrac {45 \times 40} {360} \\\\
                                                &= \dfrac {45 \times 8 \times 5} {45 \times 8} \\\\
                                                &= \dfrac {\cancel {45} \times \cancel 8 \times 5} {\cancel {45} \times \cancel 8} \\\\
                                                &= 5
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Estimate how many children would say their favorite sport was football out of the whole school of $1200$ pupils.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Estimate how many children would say their favorite sport was football out of the whole school of $1200$ pupils.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%
</div>

</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Children who liked football}              &= \dfrac {360 - 90 - 45 - 60 - 30} {360} \times 1200 \\\\

                                                &= \dfrac {\cancel 3 \times 45 \times \cancel {120} \times 10} {\cancel {120} \times \cancel 3} \\\\
                                                &= 45 \times 10 \\\\
                                                &= 450
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

I plant some seeds and get three white flowers. Write down how many blue flowers I should expect to grow.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">I plant some seeds and get three white flowers. Write down how many blue flowers I should expect to grow.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the expected number of blue flowers $= a$

Using equivalent ratio,

$
\begin{aligned}
1 \ \text{white} : 3 \ \text{blue}              &= 3 \ \text{white} : a \ \text{blue} \\\\
\dfrac{1} {3}                                   &= \dfrac {3} {a} \\\\
1 \times a                                      &= 3 \times 3 \\\\
a                                               &= 9
\end{aligned}
$

Expected number of blue flowers $= 9$
</div>
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Using ratio,

$
\begin{array}{cccccccccccccc}
  & \text{white}                  &:& \text{blue} \\\\
= & 1                             &:& 3 \\\\
= & 1 \times 3                    &:& 3 \times 3 \\\\
= & 3                             &:& 9
\end{array}
$

Expected number of blue flowers $= 9$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$9$

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

I plant a total of $30$ seeds in another patch of the garden. Calculate how many white flowers I would expect to grow in this patch.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">I plant a total of $30$ seeds in another patch of the garden. Calculate how many white flowers I would expect to grow in this patch.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the expected number of white flowers $= a$

Expected number of pink flowers $= 2a$

Expected number of blue flowers $= 3a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
a + 2a + 3a         &= 30 \\\\
6a                  &= 30 \\\\
a                   &= \dfrac {30} {6} \\\\
a                   &= \dfrac {6 \times 5} {6} \\\\
a                   &= \dfrac {\cancel 6 \times 5} {\cancel 6} \\\\
a                   &= 5
\end{aligned}
$

Expected number of white flowers $= 5$
</div>
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Using whole to part ratio,

$
\begin{array}{cccccccccccccc}
  & \text{seeds}                                      &:& \text{white} \\\\
= & 1 + 2 + 3                                         &:& 1 \\\\
= & 6                                                 &:& 1 \\\\
= & 6 \times 5                                        &:& 1 \times 5 \\\\
= & 30                                                &:& 5
\end{array}
$

Expected number of white flowers $= 5$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$5$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question_envelope rag_not_found subquestion">
<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

In another area of the garden, $24$ blue flowers are grown. Calculate how many pink flowers I should expect to find here.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">In another area of the garden, $24$ blue flowers are grown. Calculate how many pink flowers I should expect to find here.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the expected number of pink flowers $= a$

Using equivalent ratio,

$
\begin{aligned}
3 \ \text{blue} : 2 \ \text{pink}               &= 24 \ \text{blue} : a \ \text{pink} \\\\
\dfrac{3}{2}                                    &= \dfrac {24} {a} \\\\
3 \times a                                      &= 24 \times 2 \\\\
a                                               &= \dfrac {24 \times 2} {3} \\\\
a                                               &= \dfrac {8 \times 3 \times 2} {3} \\\\
a                                               &= \dfrac {8 \times \cancel 3 \times 2} {\cancel 3} \\\\
a                                               &= 8 \times 2 \\\\
a                                               &= 16
\end{aligned}
$

Expected number of pink flowers $= 16$
</div>
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Using ratio,

$
\begin{array}{cccccccccccccc}
  & \text{blue}                               &:& \text{pink} \\\\
= & 3                                         &:& 2 \\\\
= & 3 \times 8                                &:& 2 \times 8 \\\\
= & 24                                        &:& 16
\end{array}
$

Expected number of pink flowers $= 16$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$16$

</div>

**Question**

If I pick a flower at random from the $150$ grown in the test, list the following possible outcomes in order of likelihood, 
starting with the least likely:

-  picking a red or orange flower
-  picking a purple flower
-  picking an orange or yellow flower
-  picking a yellow flower

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">If I pick a flower at random from the $150$ grown in the test, list the following possible outcomes in order of likelihood, 
starting with the least likely:
<emptyline>
-  picking a red or orange flower
-  picking a purple flower
-  picking an orange or yellow flower
-  picking a yellow flower
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">

<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Probability}  = \dfrac { \text{ Favourable outcomes} } { \text{Total outcomes} }$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{red or orange flower}    &= \dfrac {20 + 58} {150} \\\\
                               &= \dfrac {78} {150} \\\\
\text{purple flower}           &= \dfrac {0} {150} \\\\
\text{orange or yellow flower} &= \dfrac {58 + 72} {150} \\\\
                               &= \dfrac {130} {150} \\\\
\text{yellow flower}           &= \dfrac {72} {150}
\end{aligned}
$

Order of likelihood

-  picking a purple flower
-  picking a yellow flower
-  picking a red or orange flower
-  picking an orange or yellow flower
</div>
</div>

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

B, D, A, C

</div>
</div>

<ul class="subquestion lower-alpha question_type_subquestion list_type_lower-alpha">
<li class="questionContainer">
<div class="question_envelope rag_not_found subquestion">
<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Write down the percentage of children who have two siblings.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Write down the percentage of children who have two siblings.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{\% of children with 2 siblings}           &= \dfrac {90} {360} \times 100 \\\\
                                                &= \dfrac {90 \times 100} {360} \\\\
                                                &= \dfrac {90 \times 4 \times 25} {90 \times 4} \\\\
                                                &= \dfrac {\cancel {90} \times \cancel 4 \times 25} {\cancel {90} \times \cancel 4} \\\\
                                                &= 25\%

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

\end{aligned}
$

**Question**

$8$ of the children who were surveyed had one sibling.

Fill in the table below to show the number of children who have $0, 2$ and $3$ siblings.

|      Number of siblings     | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ |
|:---------------------------:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| Number of children surveyed |     | $8$ |     |     |

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</code></pre>

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {45} {360} \times a          &= 8 \\\\

a                                   &= \dfrac {8 \times 360} {45} \\\\
a                                   &= \dfrac {8 \times 8 \times 45} {45} \\\\
a                                   &= \dfrac {8 \times 8 \times \cancel {45}} {\cancel {45}} \\\\
a                                   &= 8 \times 8 \\\\
a                                   &= 64
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Children with no siblings}    &= \dfrac {135} {360} \times 64 \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {135 \times 64} {360} \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {45 \times 3 \times 8 \times 8} {45 \times 8} \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {\cancel {45} \times 3 \times 8 \times \cancel 8} {\cancel {45} \times \cancel 8} \\\\
                                    &= 24 \\\\
\text{Children with 2 siblings}     &= \dfrac {90} {360} \times 64 \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {90 \times 64} {360} \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {90 \times 4 \times 16} {90 \times 4} \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {\cancel {90} \times \cancel 4 \times 16} {\cancel {90} \times \cancel 4} \\\\
                                    &= 16 \\\\
\text{Children with 3 siblings}     &= \dfrac {90} {360} \times 64 \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {90 \times 64} {360} \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {90 \times 4 \times 16} {90 \times 4} \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {\cancel {90} \times \cancel 4 \times 16} {\cancel {90} \times \cancel 4} \\\\
                                    &= 16
\end{aligned}
$

|      Number of siblings     | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ |
|:---------------------------:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| Number of children surveyed | $24$| $8$ | $16$| $16$|
</div>

<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Height of triangle ABC}   &= 5 - 3 \\\\
                                &= 2 \ \text{cm} \\\\
\text{Base of triangle ABC}     &= 6 - 0 \\\\
                                &= 6 \ \text{cm} \\\\
\text{Area of triangle ABC}     &= \dfrac {1} {2} \times \text{Height of triangle ABC} \times \text{Base of triangle ABC} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {1} {2} \times 2 \times 6 \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {2 \times 6} {2} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {\cancel 2 \times 6} {\cancel 2} \\\\
                                &= 6 \ {\text{cm}} ^ 2 \\\\
\text{Area of kite ABCD}        &= 2 \times \text{Area of triangle ABC} \\\\
                                &= 2 \times 6 \\\\
                                &= 12 \ {\text{cm}} ^ 2
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Peter walked at $4\ \text{km/h}$. 

How far is it around the school field? 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Peter walked at $4\ \text{km/h}$. 
<emptyline>
How far is it around the school field? 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
- ABBR: It is really important to use the right units in calculations and convert where required.
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text {Distance} = \text{Speed} \times \text{Time}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Distance}     &= 4 \ \text{km/h} \times \dfrac {15} {60} \ \text{h} \\\\
                    &= 4 \ \text{km/h} \times \dfrac {15} {60} \ \text{h} \\\\
                    &= \dfrac {4 \times 15} {60} \\\\
                    &= \dfrac {4 \times 15} {4 \times 15} \\\\
                    &= \dfrac {\cancel 4 \times \cancel {15}} {\cancel 4 \times \cancel {15}} \\\\
                    &= 1 \ \text{km}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$1 \ \text{km}$

</div>
</div>

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Distance}     &= 4 \ \text{km/h} \times \dfrac {15} {60} \ \text{h} \\\\
                    &= 4 \ \text{km/h} \times \dfrac {15} {60} \ \text{h} \\\\
                    &= \dfrac {4 \times 15} {60} \\\\
                    &= \dfrac {4 \times 15} {4 \times 15} \\\\
                    &= \dfrac {\cancel 4 \times \cancel {15}} {\cancel 4 \times \cancel {15}} \\\\
                    &= 1 \ \text{km}
\end{aligned}
$
</code></pre>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

A sheet of graph paper is placed with its $x$-axis pointing due East and its $y$-axis pointing due North. 
A sluggish snail starts at point $(0, 0)$ and slowly, 
but smoothly, slithers $1$ unit North, $2$ units East, $3$ units South, $4$ units West, 
$5$ units North, $6$ units East, $7$ units South, $8$ units West, $9$ units North and (lastly!) $10$ units East. 

At which point does the snail finally arrive? 

</div>

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

**Working**

TODO: not correct do. based on graph

Let the amount of kroner I get $= a$

Using equivalent ratio,

$
\begin{aligned}
100 \ \text{pence} : 18 \ \text{kroner}         &= 90 \ \text{pence} : a \ \text{kroner} \\\\
\dfrac{100} {18}                                &= \dfrac {90} {a} \\\\
100a                                            &= 90 \times 18 \\\\
a                                               &= \dfrac {90 \times 18} {100} \\\\
a                                               &= \dfrac {1620} {100} \\\\
a                                               &= 16.2 \ \text{kroner}
\end{aligned}
$

Answer $= 16.2 \ \text{kroner}$
</div>
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$
\begin{array}{cccccccccccccc}
  & \text{pence}                   &:& \text{kroner} \\\\
= & 100                            &:& 18 \\\\
= & 1                              &:& \dfrac {18} {100} \\\\
= & 1 \times 90                    &:& \dfrac {18 \times 90} {100} \\\\
= & 90                             &:& \dfrac {1620} {100} \\\\
= & 90 \text{pence}                &:& 16.2 \ \text{kroner}
\end{array}
$

Answer $= 16.2 \ \text{kroner}$

**Question**

How much are $12 \ \text{kroner}$ worth? 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">How much are $12 \ \text{kroner}$ worth? 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%
</div>

<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the amount of pounds I get $= a$

Using equivalent ratio,

$
\begin{aligned}
18 \ \text{kroner} : \pounds 1                  &= 12 \ \text{kroner} : \pounds a \\\\
18                                              &= \dfrac {12} {a} \\\\
18a                                             &= 12 \\\\
a                                               &= \dfrac {12} {18} \\\\
a                                               &= \dfrac {6 \times 2} {6 \times 3} \\\\
a                                               &= \dfrac {\cancel 6 \times 2} {\cancel 6 \times 3} \\\\
a                                               &= \pounds \dfrac {2} {3}
\end{aligned}
$

Answer $= \pounds \dfrac {2} {3}$
</div>
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

= & 12                             &:& \dfrac {6 \times 2} {6 \times 3} \\\\
= & 12                             &:& \dfrac {\cancel 6 \times 2} {\cancel 6 \times 3} \\\\
= & 12 \ \text{kroner}             &:& \pounds \dfrac {2} {3}
\end{array}
$

Answer $= \pounds \dfrac {2} {3}$
</div>

<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the value in kroner $= a$

Using equivalent ratio,

$
\begin{aligned}
\pounds 1 : 18 \ \text{kroner}                  &= \pounds 5.1 : a \ \text{kroner} \\\\
\dfrac{1} {18}                                  &= \dfrac {5.1} {a} \\\\
a                                               &= 5.1 \times 18 \\\\
a                                               &= 91.8 \ \text{kroner}
\end{aligned}
$

Answer $= 91.8 \ \text{kroner}$
</div>

\end{array}
$

Answer $= 91.8 \ \text{kroner}$

children's heights were recorded on a chart. (The last $6$ names are the girls names.)

- If Barry grew another $1 \ \text{cm}$ he would be the same height as the tallest girl.
- Steven is $20 \ \text{cm}$ taller than the shortest boy.

**Question**

What is the difference in height between the shortest member of the club and the tallest member?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">What is the difference in height between the shortest member of the club and the tallest member?
</code></pre>

<div class="workings">

</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Range} = \text{Highest number} - \text{Lowest number}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Height of Tina}  &= 127 \ \text{cm} \\\\
\text {Height of Faye}  &= 146 - 20 \\\\
                        &= 126 \ \text{cm} \\\\
\text {Height of Barry} &= 137 - 1 \\\\
                        &= 136 \ \text{cm} \\\\
\text {Height of Steven}&= 122 + 20 \\\\
                        &= 142 \ \text{cm} \\\\
\text {Difference}      &= 146 - 113 \\\\
                        &= 33 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

                                        &= \dfrac {\cancel {25} \times \cancel 4 \times 24} {\cancel {25} \times \cancel 4} \\\\
                                        &= 24
\end{aligned}
$

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number of games won $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
a + a + 24              &= 96 \\\\
2a + 24                 &= 96 \\\\
2a                      &= 96 - 24 \\\\
2a                      &= 72 \\\\
a                       &= \dfrac {72} {2} \\\\
a                       &= \dfrac {2 \times 36} {2} \\\\
a                       &= \dfrac {\cancel 2 \times 36} {\cancel 2} \\\\
a                       &= 36
\end{aligned}
$

Number of games won $= 36$
</div>

**Question**

It was found that $12$ walked to school.

How many pupils took a car to school?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">It was found that $12$ walked to school.
<emptyline>
How many pupils took a car to school?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the total number of people $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {135} {360} \times a         &= 12 \\\\
a                                   &= 12 \times \dfrac {360} {135} \\\\
a                                   &= \dfrac {12 \times 360} {135} \\\\
a                                   &= \dfrac {4 \times 3 \times 45 \times 8} {45 \times 3} \\\\
a                                   &= \dfrac {4 \times \cancel 3 \times \cancel {45} \times 8} {\cancel {45} \times \cancel 3} \\\\
a                                   &= 4 \times 8 \\\\
a                                   &= 32
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Number of people who go by car}     &= \dfrac {90} {360} \times 32 \\\\
                                          &= \dfrac {90 \times 32} {360} \\\\
                                          &= \dfrac {90 \times 4 \times 8} {90 \times 4} \\\\
                                          &= \dfrac {\cancel {90} \times \cancel 4 \times 8} {\cancel {90} \times \cancel 4} \\\\
                                          &= 8
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Using ratio,

$
\begin{array}{cccccccccccccc}
  & \text{walk}                                 &:& \text{car} \\\\
= & 135                                         &:& 90 \\\\
= & 1                                           &:& \dfrac {90} {135} \\\\
= & 1 \times 12                                 &:& \dfrac {90} {135} \times 12 \\\\
= & 12                                          &:& \dfrac {90 \times 12} {135} \\\\
= & 12                                          &:& \dfrac {45 \times 2 \times 3 \times 4} {45 \times 3} \\\\
= & 12                                          &:& \dfrac {\cancel {45} \times 2 \times \cancel 3 \times 4} {\cancel {45} \times \cancel 3} \\\\
= & 12                                          &:& 2 \times 4 \\\\
= & 12                                          &:& 8
\end{array}
$

Number of pupils who took a car to school $= 8$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$8$

**Question**

How many pupils did not catch the train to school?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">How many pupils did not catch the train to school?
</code></pre>

<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="tip">

</div>

<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Using value from the answer above,

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Number of people who did not catch the train}     &= \dfrac {360 - 45} {360} \times 32 \\\\
                                                        &= \dfrac {315} {360} \times 32 \\\\
                                                        &= \dfrac {315 \times 32} {360} \\\\
                                                        &= \dfrac {45 \times 7 \times 8 \times 4} {45 \times 8} \\\\
                                                        &= \dfrac {\cancel {45} \times 7 \times \cancel 8 \times 4} {\cancel {45} \times \cancel 8} \\\\
                                                        &= 7 \times 4 \\\\
                                                        &= 28
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Using ratio,

$
\begin{array}{cccccccccccccc}
  & \text{walk}                                 &:& \text{not train} \\\\
= & 135                                         &:& 360 - 45 \\\\
= & 135                                         &:& 315 \\\\
= & 1                                           &:& \dfrac {315} {135} \\\\

**Question**

In an attempt to improve the environment children are encouraged to find a “greener” way to get to school. A third of those who travel by car decide to walk and $3$ move from bus to walking too. How many now walk?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">In an attempt to improve the environment children are encouraged to find a “greener” way to get to school. A third of those who travel by car decide to walk and $3$ move from bus to walking too. How many now walk?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Number of children}           &= 14 + \dfrac {1} {3} \times 15 + 3 \\\\
                                    &= 14 + \dfrac {15} {3} + 3 \\\\
                                    &= 14 + \dfrac {5 \times 3} {3} + 3 \\\\
                                    &= 14 + \dfrac {5 \times \cancel 3} {\cancel 3} + 3 \\\\
                                    &= 14 + 5 + 3 \\\\
                                    &= 22
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

|            $6$                |       $10$        |                           |
|            $7$                |       $3$         |                           |

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

\text{Black cars}               &= \dfrac {90} {360} \times 120 \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {90 \times 120} {360} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {3 \times 30 \times 120} {120 \times 3} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {\cancel 3 \times 30 \times \cancel {120}} {\cancel {120} \times \cancel 3} \\\\
                                &= 30
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

How many students favourite colour is Green? 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">How many students favourite colour is Green? 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Students who prefer green}    &= \dfrac {1} {4} \times 32 \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {32} {4} \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {4 \times 8} {4} \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {\cancel{4} \times 8} {\cancel{4}} \\\\
                                    &= 8
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$8$

</div>
</div>
<div class="workingscodeblock">
<div class="tipcodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

                                    &= \dfrac {32} {4} \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {4 \times 8} {4} \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {\cancel{4} \times 8} {\cancel{4}} \\\\
                                    &= 8

$

**Question**

How many students favourite colour is NOT Blue?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">How many students favourite colour is NOT Blue?
</code></pre>

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Note: **NOT** selecting blue is same as selecting any of the other colours instead.

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Not blue}     &= \bigg(\dfrac {1} {4} + \dfrac {1} {4} + \dfrac {1} {8} \bigg) \times 32 \\\\
                    &= \bigg(\dfrac {1 \times 2} {4 \times 2} + \dfrac {1 \times 2} {4 \times 2} + \dfrac {1} {8} \bigg) \times 32 \\\\
                    &= \bigg(\dfrac {2} {8} + \dfrac {2} {8} + \dfrac {1} {8} \bigg) \times 32 \\\\
                    &= \dfrac {5} {8} \times 32 \\\\
                    &= \dfrac {5 \times 32} {8} \\\\
                    &= \dfrac {5 \times 8 \times 4} {8} \\\\
                    &= \dfrac {5 \times \cancel{8} \times 4} {\cancel{8}} \\\\
                    &= 5 \times 4 \\\\
                    &= 20
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$20$

Let the coordinates $= (a, b)$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {1 + a} {2}            &= 7 \\\\
1 + a                         &= 7 \times 2 \\\\
1 + a                         &= 14 \\\\
a                             &= 14 - 1 \\\\
a                             &= 13 \\\\
\dfrac {4 + b} {2}            &= 1 \\\\
4 + b                         &= 1 \times 2 \\\\
4 + b                         &= 2 \\\\
b                             &= 2 - 4 \\\\
b                             &= -2
\end{aligned}
$

Coordinates $= (13, -2)$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

$40$ children predicted who would win the boys' Call of Duty competition. 

The pie chart below shows their predictions.

![papers/sevenoaks-school/2011/sample-paper-2/s01-q11-i00.png](/assets/papers/sevenoaks-school/2011/sample-paper-2/s01-q11-i00.png "papers/sevenoaks-school/2011/sample-paper-2/s01-q11-i00.png")

How many children predicted that Stefan would win?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">$40$ children predicted who would win the boys' Call of Duty competition. 
<emptyline>
The pie chart below shows their predictions.
<emptyline>
%image%
<emptyline>
How many children predicted that Stefan would win?
</code></pre>
</div>

<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>
</div>

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Angle of Stefan sector}     &= 90 - 5 \% \text{ of } 360 \\\\
                                  &= 90 - \dfrac {5} {100} \times 360 \\\\
                                  &= 90 - \dfrac {5 \times 360} {100} \\\\
                                  &= 90 - \dfrac {5 \times 20 \times 18} {5 \times 20} \\\\
                                  &= 90 - \dfrac {\cancel 5 \times \cancel {20} \times 18} {\cancel 5 \times \cancel {20}} \\\\
                                  &= 90 - 18 \\\\
                                  &= 72 \degree \\\\
\text{Number of children}         &= \dfrac {72} {360} \times 40 \\\\
                                  &= \dfrac {72 \times 40} {360} \\\\
                                  &= \dfrac {8 \times 9 \times 40} {9 \times 40} \\\\
                                  &= \dfrac {8 \times \cancel 9 \times \cancel {40}} {\cancel 9 \times \cancel {40}} \\\\
                                  &= 8
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

</code></pre>

<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

We have to reflect through a vertical line therefore y-coordinates will remain the same,

and x-coordinates of reflected points will be at the same distance as the original points but on the other side

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Distance of point with abscissa 3}    &= 20 - 3 \\\\
                                              &= 17 \\\\
\text{Corresponding reflected abscissa}       &= 20 + 17 \\\\
                                              &= 37 \\\\
\text{Distance of point with abscissa 5}    &= 20 - 5 \\\\
                                              &= 15 \\\\
\text{Corresponding reflected abscissa}       &= 20 + 15 \\\\
                                              &= 35
\end{aligned}
$

$(35, 3), (37, 3), (35, 5), (37, 5)$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$(35, 3), (37, 3), (35, 5), (37, 5)$

</div>
</div>

<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

<div class="workings">

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Height of triangle}     &= 6 - 2 \\\\
                              &= 4 \\\\
\text{Base of triangle}       &= 6 - 4 \\\\
                              &= 2 \\\\
\text{Area of triangle}       &= \dfrac {1} {2} \times \text{Height of triangle ABC} \times \text{Base of triangle ABC} \\\\
                              &= \dfrac {1} {2} \times 4 \times 2 \\\\
                              &= \dfrac {4 \times 2} {2} \\\\
                              &= \dfrac {4 \times \cancel 2} {\cancel 2} \\\\
                              &= 4
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

![papers/st-georges-college/sample/sample-paper-2/s01-q19-i00.png](/assets/papers/st-georges-college/sample/sample-paper-2/s01-q19-i00.png "papers/st-georges-college/sample/sample-paper-2/s01-q19-i00.png")

The pie chart shows the proportions of different colours of cars in a school carpark. There were $36$ black cars. How many blue cars were there?   

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">%image%
<emptyline>
The pie chart shows the proportions of different colours of cars in a school carpark. There were $36$ black cars. How many blue cars were there?   
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Using ratio,

$
\begin{array}{cccccccccccccc}
  & \text{black}                             &:& \text{blue} \\\\
= & 40 \%                                    &:& 30 \% \\\\
= & 1                                        &:& \dfrac {30} {40} \\\\
= & 1 \times 36                              &:& \dfrac {30 \times 36} {40} \\\\
= & 36                                       &:& \dfrac {3 \times 10 \times 4 \times 9} {4 \times 10} \\\\
= & 36                                       &:& \dfrac {3 \times \cancel {10} \times \cancel 4 \times 9} {\cancel 4 \times \cancel {10}} \\\\
= & 36                                       &:& 3 \times 9 \\\\
= & 36                                       &:& 27
\end{array}
$

Number of blue cars $= 36$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$36$

</div>
</div>
<div class="workingscodeblock">
<div class="tipcodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Using ratio,

  & \text{black}                             &:& \text{blue} \\\\
= & 40 \%                                    &:& 30 \% \\\\
= & 1                                        &:& \dfrac {30} {40} \\\\
= & 1 \times 36                              &:& \dfrac {30 \times 36} {40} \\\\
= & 36                                       &:& \dfrac {3 \times 10 \times 4 \times 9} {4 \times 10} \\\\
= & 36                                       &:& \dfrac {3 \times \cancel {10} \times \cancel 4 \times 9} {\cancel 4 \times \cancel {10}} \\\\
= & 36                                       &:& 3 \times 9 \\\\
= & 36                                       &:& 27
\end{array}
$
<emptyline>
Number of blue cars $= 36$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

The chart below shows the mileage between five places in North London. For example it gives the distance between Kenton and 
Hampstead as $4 \ \text{miles}$.

![papers/the-haberdashers-askes-boys-school/2011/sample-paper-3/s01-q16-i00.png](/assets/papers/the-haberdashers-askes-boys-school/2011/sample-paper-3/s01-q16-i00.png "papers/the-haberdashers-askes-boys-school/2011/sample-paper-3/s01-q16-i00.png")

Daisy lives in Hampstead and drives her son to school at Haberdashers' in the morning before continuing on to the office in Southgate. 
She then visits her sister in Harpenden before driving home via Habs. How far does she travel altogether?

</div>

<li class="questionContainer">
<div class="question_envelope rag_not_found subquestion">
<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

The y-coordinate of the centre of one of the squares in this sequence is $2177$. Work out the x-coordinate of this square.

![papers/the-haberdashers-askes-boys-school/2011/sample-paper-3/s01-q28-s05-i00.png](/assets/papers/the-haberdashers-askes-boys-school/2011/sample-paper-3/s01-q28-s05-i00.png "papers/the-haberdashers-askes-boys-school/2011/sample-paper-3/s01-q28-s05-i00.png")

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">The y-coordinate of the centre of one of the squares in this sequence is $2177$. Work out the x-coordinate of this square.
<emptyline>
%image%
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the x-coordinate $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
2 \times a - 1      &= 2177 \\\\
2a - 1              &= 2177 \\\\
2a                  &= 2177 + 1 \\\\
2a                  &= 2178 \\\\
a                   &= \dfrac {2178} {2} \\\\
a                   &= \dfrac {2 \times 1089} {2} \\\\
a                   &= \dfrac {\cancel 2 \times 1089} {\cancel 2} \\\\
a                   &= 1089
\end{aligned}
$

X-coordinate of the center of the square $= 1089$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

If $45$ people chose Athletics, how many chose Hockey?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

</code></pre>

<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Using ratio,

$
\begin{array}{cccccccccccccc}
  & \text{athletics}                        &:& \text{hockey} \\\\
= & 36                                      &:& 12 \\\\
= & 1                                       &:& \dfrac {12} {36} \\\\
= & 1 \times 45                             &:& \dfrac {12 \times 45} {36} \\\\
= & 45                                      &:& \dfrac {12 \times 15 \times 3} {12 \times 3} \\\\
= & 45                                      &:& \dfrac {\cancel {12} \times 15 \times \cancel 3} {\cancel {12} \times \cancel 3} \\\\
= & 45                                      &:& 15
\end{array}
$

Number of people who choose $= 15$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$15$

</div>
</div>

**Question**

The average rainfall for the first three months of the year is

$\dfrac{50 + 40 + 35}{3} = \dfrac{125}{3} = 41 \dfrac{2}{3} \ \text{mm}$

Work out the average rainfall for the last three months. Give your answer as a mixed fraction.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

\end{aligned}
$
</div>

**Question**

Peter buys $1500$ shares in $2009$ and sells them in a later year. Given that he makes a loss of $\pounds 3000$, 
find the two possible years in which he might have sold his shares.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Peter buys $1500$ shares in $2009$ and sells them in a later year. Given that he makes a loss of $\pounds 3000$, 
find the two possible years in which he might have sold his shares.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%

</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Loss per share}       &= \dfrac {3000} {1500} \\\\
                              &= \dfrac {1500 \times 2} {1500} \\\\
                              &= \dfrac {\cancel {1500} \times 2} {\cancel {1500}} \\\\
                              &= \pounds 2 \\\\
\text{Selling price of share} &= 6 - 2\\\\
                              &= \pounds 4
\end{aligned}
$

Two possible years $= 2010, 2014$
</div>
</div>

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

                                    &= \dfrac {33 \dfrac {1} {3}} {100} \times 360 \\\\

                                    &= \dfrac {\cancel {100} \times \cancel 3 \times 120} {\cancel 3 \times \cancel {100}} \\\\
                                    &= 120 \degree
\end{aligned}
$
