An empty jug is filled with water at a constant rate. The graph shows how the height, $h$ of the level of water varies over time, 
$t$, as the jug fills up.

**Question**

What is the area of shape $A$?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">What is the area of shape $A$?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="tip">

</div>

<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Height of the triangle}   &= 2 - 1 \\\\
                                &= 1 \\\\
\text{Base of the triangle}     &= 5 - 2 \\\\
                                &= 3 \\\\
\text{Area of the triangle}     &= \dfrac {1} {2} \times \text{Height of the triangle} \times \text{Base of the triangle} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {1} {2} \times 1 \times 3 \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {3} {2} \\\\
\text{Area of the triangle}     &= 2 \times \text{Area of the triangle} \\\\
                                &= 2 \times \dfrac {3} {2} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {2 \times 3} {2} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {\cancel 2 \times 3} {\cancel 2} \\\\
                                &= 3
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$3$

</div>

**Question**

Mark has $40$ counters in his bag.

How many of his counters are not blue?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Mark has $40$ counters in his bag.
<emptyline>
How many of his counters are not blue?
</code></pre>

<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Using value from the answer above,

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Number of counters that are not blue}   &= (100 - 25) \% \ \text{of} \ 40 \\\\
                                              &= 75 \% \ \text{of} \ 40 \\\\
                                              &= \dfrac {75} {100} \times 40 \\\\
                                              &= \dfrac {75 \times 40} {100} \\\\
                                              &= \dfrac {25 \times 3 \times 4 \times 10} {25 \times 4} \\\\
                                              &= \dfrac {\cancel {25} \times 3 \times \cancel 4 \times 10} {\cancel {25} \times \cancel 4} \\\\
                                              &= 3 \times 10 \\\\
                                              &= 30
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$30$

**Question**

$\dfrac{1}{3}$ of Sarah's counters are red, and the rest are green or blue.

Given that Sarah has $12$ red counters, how many counters are there altogether in her bag?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>

<emptyline>
Given that Sarah has $12$ red counters, how many counters are there altogether in her bag?
</code></pre>
</div>

<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {1} {3} \times a       &= 12 \\\\
\dfrac {a} {3}                &= 12 \\\\
a                             &= 12 \times 3 \\\\
a                             &= 36
\end{aligned}
$

Total number of counters Sarah has $= 36$
</div>

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$36$

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Sarah has twice as many green counters as blue ones. 

How many blue counters does she have?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Sarah has twice as many green counters as blue ones. 
<emptyline>
How many blue counters does she have?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number of blue counters Sarah has $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
a + 2a + 12         &= 36 \\\\
3a + 12             &= 36 \\\\
3a                  &= 36 - 12 \\\\
3a                  &= 24 \\\\
a                   &= \dfrac {24} {3} \\\\
a                   &= \dfrac {3 \times 8} {3} \\\\
a                   &= \dfrac {\cancel 3 \times 8} {\cancel 3} \\\\
a                   &= 8
\end{aligned}
$

Number of blue counters Sarah has $= 8$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$8$

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Probability of picking green counter from Mark's bag}     &= \dfrac {180} {360} \\\\
                                                                &= \dfrac {180} {180 \times 2} \\\\
                                                                &= \dfrac {\cancel {180}} {\cancel {180} \times 2} \\\\
                                                                &= 0.5 \\\\
\text{Probability of picking green counter from Sarah's bag}    &= \dfrac {8} {36} \\\\
                                                                &= \dfrac {4 \times 2} {4 \times 9} \\\\
                                                                &= \dfrac {\cancel 4 \times 2} {\cancel 4 \times 9} \\\\
                                                                &= \dfrac {2} {9} \\\\
                                                                &= 0.22
\end{aligned}
$

Mark is more likely to pick a green counter.
</div>
</div>

Mark

**Question**

Sarah measured the temperature of the beaker again $4 \ \text{hours}$ and $30 \ \text{minutes}$ after the last reading on the graph.

At what time did she take this measurement?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Sarah measured the temperature of the beaker again $4 \ \text{hours}$ and $30 \ \text{minutes}$ after the last reading on the graph.
<emptyline>
At what time did she take this measurement?
</code></pre>

<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
- ABBR: It is really important to use the right units in calculations and convert where required.
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Time when she took the reading}   &= 10 {:} 50 \ \text{am} + 4 \ \text{hours} \ 30 \ \text{min} \\\\
                                        &= 10 {:} 50 \ \text{am} + 4 \times 60 \ \text{min} + 30 \ \text{min} \\\\
                                        &= 10 {:} 50 \ \text{am} + 4 \times 60 + 30 \\\\
                                        &= 10 {:} 50 + 240 + 30 \\\\
                                        &= 10 {:} 50 + 270 \\\\
                                        &= 3 {:} 20 \ \text{pm}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$3 {:} 20 \ \text{pm}$

</div>

</code></pre>

<div class="workingcodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Working Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Time when she took the reading}   &= 10 {:} 50 \ \text{am} + 4 \ \text{hours} \ 30 \ \text{min} \\\\
                                        &= 10 {:} 50 \ \text{am} + 4 \times 60 \ \text{min} + 30 \ \text{min} \\\\
                                        &= 10 {:} 50 \ \text{am} + 4 \times 60 + 30 \\\\
                                        &= 10 {:} 50 + 240 + 30 \\\\
                                        &= 10 {:} 50 + 270 \\\\
                                        &= 3 {:} 20 \ \text{pm}
\end{aligned}
$
</code></pre>

**Question**

How many pupils chose Comedy?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Pupils who chose comedy}              &= \dfrac {90} {360} \times 72 \\\\
                                            &= \dfrac {90 \times 72} {360} \\\\
                                            &= \dfrac {90 \times 4 \times 18} {90 \times 4} \\\\
                                            &= \dfrac {\cancel {90} \times \cancel 4 \times 18} {\cancel {90} \times \cancel 4} \\\\
                                            &= 18
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

                            &= 8
\end{aligned}
$

<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

</code></pre>

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the total number of pets $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {120} {360} \times a     &= 48 \\\\
a                               &= 48 \times \dfrac {360} {120} \\\\
a                               &= \dfrac {48 \times 360} {120} \\\\
a                               &= \dfrac {48 \times 120 \times 3} {120} \\\\
a                               &= \dfrac {48 \times \cancel {120} \times 3} {\cancel {120}} \\\\
a                               &= 48 \times 3 \\\\
a                               &= 144
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Number of hamsters}       &= \dfrac {60} {360} \times 144 \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {60 \times 144} {360} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {60 \times 6 \times 24} {60 \times 6} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {\cancel {60} \times \cancel 6 \times 24} {\cancel {60} \times \cancel 6} \\\\
                                &= 24
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

= & 48                                      &:& \dfrac {60 \times 48} {120} \\\\
= & 48                                      &:& \dfrac {60 \times 2 \times 24} {60 \times 2} \\\\
= & 48                                      &:& \dfrac {\cancel {60} \times \cancel 2 \times 24} {\cancel {60} \times \cancel 2} \\\\
= & 48                                      &:& 24
\end{array}
$

Number of hamsters $= 24$

**Question**

What percentage of girls have brown hair?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">What percentage of girls have brown hair?
</code></pre>

<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%
</div>

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{\% of girl with brown hair}               &= \dfrac {9 + 15} {11 + 15 + 9 + 10 + 5} \times 100 \\\\
                                                &= \dfrac {24} {50} \times 100 \\\\
                                                &= \dfrac {24 \times 100} {50} \\\\
                                                &= \dfrac {24 \times 50 \times 2} {50} \\\\
                                                &= \dfrac {24 \times \cancel {50} \times 2} {\cancel {50}} \\\\
                                                &= 24 \times 2 \\\\
                                                &= 48 \%
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$48 \%$

</div>
</div>

                                            &= \dfrac {\cancel {2} \times 25 \times \cancel {4}} {\cancel {2} \times \cancel {4}} \\\\
                                            &= 25 \%
\end{aligned}
$

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

$24$ people said that they liked Dorothy best.

How many more people liked Dorothy than the Scarecrow?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">$24$ people said that they liked Dorothy best.
<emptyline>
How many more people liked Dorothy than the Scarecrow?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the total number of people $=a$

Number of people that liked scarecrow $=\dfrac{a}{8}$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {4} {8} \ \text {of} \ a                 &= 24 \\\\
\dfrac {4} {8} \times a                         &= 24 \\\\
a                                               &= \dfrac {24 \times 8} {4} \\\\
a                                               &= \dfrac {24 \times 4 \times 2} {4} \\\\
a                                               &= \dfrac {24 \times \cancel{4} \times 2} {\cancel{4}} \\\\
a                                               &= 24 \times  2 \\\\
a                                               &= 48
\end{aligned}
$

Total number of people $= 48$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{People that liked scarecrow}              &= \dfrac{a}{8} \\\\
                                                &= \dfrac{48}{8} \\\\
                                                &= \dfrac {6 \times 8} {8} \\\\
                                                &= \dfrac {6 \times \cancel{8}} {\cancel{8}} \\\\
                                                &= 6 \\\\
\text {Difference}                              &= 24 - 6 \\\\
                                                &= 18
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$18$

</div>
</div>

Total number of children in class $= 24$

How many more children chose athletics than gymnastics?

\end{aligned}
$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Five children took exams in English and Maths.

Their names are Dolly, Holly, Lolly, Molly and Polly.

The bar chart below shows their results.

![papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2013/group-1/s01-q37-i00.png](/assets/papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2013/group-1/s01-q37-i00.png "papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2013/group-1/s01-q37-i00.png")

Use the information below to work out which child is represented by each letter.

- Dolly came top in the Maths exam.
- In the English exam, it was Molly who scored the highest.
- Polly got the lowest total score.
- Holly scored $30$ more marks in English than she did in Maths.

</div>

                        &= \dfrac {24 + 8} {4} \\\\
                        &= \dfrac {32} {4} \\\\
                        &= \dfrac {8 \times 4} {4} \\\\
                        &= \dfrac {8 \times \cancel 4} {\cancel 4} \\\\
                        &= 8 \\\\
\text{y-coordinates}    &= \dfrac {3 \times 0 + 1 \times 8} {3 + 1} \\\\
                        &= \dfrac {0 + 8} {4} \\\\
                        &= \dfrac {8} {4} \\\\
                        &= \dfrac {2 \times 4} {4} \\\\
                        &= \dfrac {2 \times \cancel 4} {\cancel 4} \\\\
                        &= 2
\end{aligned}
$

Coordinates $= (8, 2)$
</div>
</div>

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Fraction  who said Brie}              &= \dfrac {30} {360} \\\\
                                            &= \dfrac {30} {30 \times 12} \\\\

<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

**Working**

Let the total number of people $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
a \times \dfrac {90} {360}    &= 18 \\\\
a                             &= 18 \times \dfrac {360} {90} \\\\
a                             &= \dfrac {18 \times 360} {90} \\\\
a                             &= \dfrac {18 \times 90 \times 4} {90} \\\\
a                             &= \dfrac {18 \times \cancel {90} \times 4} {\cancel {90}} \\\\
a                             &= 18 \times 4 \\\\
a                             &= 72
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Number of people who said Goat's cheese}    &= \dfrac {30} {360} \times 72 \\\\
                                                  &= \dfrac {30 \times 72} {360} \\\\
                                                  &= \dfrac {5 \times 6 \times 72} {72 \times 5} \\\\
                                                  &= \dfrac {\cancel 5 \times 6 \times \cancel {72}} {\cancel {72} \times \cancel 5} \\\\
                                                  &= 6
\end{aligned}
$

= & \dfrac {18 \times \cancel 5} {\cancel 5}    &:& \dfrac {6 \times \cancel 5} {\cancel 5} \\\\
= & 18                                          &:& 6
\end{array}
$

Number of people who said Goat's cheese $= 6$

$

\dfrac {2a + 7} {2 + 1}       &= 9 \\\\

a                             &= \dfrac {20} {2} \\\\
a                             &= \dfrac {2 \times 10} {2} \\\\
a                             &= \dfrac {\cancel 2 \times 10} {\cancel 2} \\\\
a                             &= 10 \\\\
\dfrac {2b + 8} {2 + 1}       &= 4 \\\\
\dfrac {2b + 8} {3}           &= 4 \\\\
2b + 8                        &= 4 \times 3 \\\\
2b + 8                        &= 12 \\\\

b                             &= \dfrac {4} {2} \\\\
b                             &= \dfrac {2 \times 2} {2} \\\\
b                             &= \dfrac {\cancel 2 \times 2} {\cancel 2} \\\\
b                             &= 2
\end{aligned}
$

Coordinates $= (10, 2)$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

<div class="workings">

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Time spent sleeping}      &= \dfrac {4.5} {12} \times 24 \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {4.5 \times 24} {12} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {4.5 \times 12 \times 2} {12} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {4.5 \times \cancel {12} \times 2} {\cancel {12}} \\\\
                                &= 4.5 \times 2 \\\\
                                &= 9 \ \text{hours}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$9 \ \text{hours}$

</div>
</div>
<div class="workingscodeblock">

Di and Ed make up two games, based on Di's results.
Tick the relevant box in the table below to say who is most likely to win, or whether there is an equal chance.

| game | rules                                                                                        | Di most likely to win | Ed most likely win | equally likely |
|:----:|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------|--------------------|----------------|
|   A  | Di scores a point if the total thrown is even. <br /> Ed scores a point if the total thrown is odd. |                       |                    |                |
|   B  | Di scores a point if the total thrown is $8$ to $12$ inclusive. <br /> Ed scores a point otherwise.     |                       |                    |                |

</div>

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Charlotte removes a third of the woodlice from pot $B$ and $20\%$ of the woodlice from pot $C$. 
She puts these woodlice under a new pot, $F$.

How many woodlice are under pot $F$?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Charlotte removes a third of the woodlice from pot $B$ and $20\%$ of the woodlice from pot $C$. 
She puts these woodlice under a new pot, $F$.
<emptyline>
How many woodlice are under pot $F$?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Woodlice under pot F}             &= \dfrac {1} {3} \times 4.5 \times 2 + 20 \% \times 5 \times 2  \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {1} {3} \times 9 + \dfrac {20} {100} \times 10  \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {9} {3} + \dfrac {20 \times 10} {100} \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {3 \times 3} {3} + \dfrac {20 \times 10} {100} \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {3 \times \cancel 3} {\cancel 3} + \dfrac {2 \cancel 0 \times 1 \cancel 0} {1 \cancel 0 \cancel 0} \\\\
                                        &= 3 + 2 \\\\
                                        &= 5
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$5$

</div>

**Question**

![papers/the-manchester-grammar-school/2012/arithmetic-2/s01-q12-i00.png](/assets/papers/the-manchester-grammar-school/2012/arithmetic-2/s01-q12-i00.png "papers/the-manchester-grammar-school/2012/arithmetic-2/s01-q12-i00.png")

A point is described by its coordinates, eg point $\text{B}$ on the diagram has coordinates $(9,8)$. This is not the same as $(8,9)$. Point $\text{A}$ has coordinates $(0,0)$.

To move from one point to another on the graph you can travel by $\text{K}$-steps or by $\text{T}$-steps.

A $\text{K}$-step moves you $1$ place to the right and $2$ places up.

A $\text{T}$-step moves you $3$ places to the right and $1$ place up.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

</div>

<emptyline>

<emptyline>
A $\text{K}$-step moves you $1$ place to the right and $2$ places up.
<emptyline>
A $\text{T}$-step moves you $3$ places to the right and $1$ place up.
</code></pre>

**Question**

It is possible to move from point $\text{A}$ to point $\text{B}$ by combining some $\text{K}$-steps and some $\text{T}$-steps.

Write down how many $\text{K}$-steps and $\text{T}$-steps are needed.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">It is possible to move from point $\text{A}$ to point $\text{B}$ by combining some $\text{K}$-steps and some $\text{T}$-steps.
<emptyline>
Write down how many $\text{K}$-steps and $\text{T}$-steps are needed.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="tip">

</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number of K step $= a$

Let the number of T step $= b$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
a + 3b    &= 9    &  (1) \\\\
2a + b    &= 8    &  (2)
\end{aligned}
$

Lets subtract equation $2$ from twice of equation $1$ to get the value of b.

$
\begin{aligned}
2 \times (a + 3b) - (2a + b)      &= 2 \times 9 - 8 \\\\
2a + 6b - 2a - b                  &= 18 - 8 \\\\
2a - 2a + 6b - b                  &= 10 \\\\
5b                                &= 10 \\\\
b                                 &= \dfrac {10} {5} \\\\
b                                 &= \dfrac {5 \times 2} {5} \\\\
b                                 &= \dfrac {\cancel 5 \times 2} {\cancel 5} \\\\
b                                 &= 2
\end{aligned}
$

Lets substitute value of b in equation $1$ to get the value of a.

$
\begin{aligned}
a + 3b            &= 9 \\\\
a + 3 \times 2    &= 9 \\\\
a + 6             &= 9 \\\\
a                 &= 9 - 6 \\\\
a                 &= 3
\end{aligned}
$

$3$ K-steps

$2$ T-steps
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$K$-step $=$ $3$

</div>
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$T$-step $=$ $2$

</div>
</div>

Megaprint make small business cards with names and contact details on, that people can give to clients as part of their work. The total cost of buying the cards they sell is made up of two amounts.

There is a fixed cost that people must pay no matter how many cards they order and this amount is always the same. Then there is a second amount which depends on the number of cards ordered. These two amounts are added together to give the total cost of the order and the graph below shows what the total cost would be for the number of cards ordered.

<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">If $200$ cards are ordered, using the total cost what is the cost of one card?
</code></pre>

<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Cost of 1 card}   &= \pounds \dfrac {10} {200} \\\\

                        &= \dfrac {5 \times \cancel 2 \times \cancel {100}} {\cancel 2 \times \cancel {100}} \\\\
                        &= 5 \ \text{p}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number of cards $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {3} {100} \times a + 4                               &= \dfrac {16 - 6} {500} \times a + 6 \\\\
\dfrac {3a} {100} + 4                                       &= \dfrac {10} {500} \times a + 6 \\\\
\dfrac {3a} {100} + 4                                       &= \dfrac {10a} {500} + 6 \\\\
\dfrac {3a} {100} - \dfrac {10a} {500}                      &= 6 - 4 \\\\
\dfrac {3a \times 5} {100 \times 5} - \dfrac {10a} {500}    &= 2 \\\\
\dfrac {15a} {500} - \dfrac {10a} {500}                     &= 2 \\\\
\dfrac {15a - 10a} {500}                                    &= 2 \\\\
\dfrac {5a} {500}                                           &= 2 \\\\
a                                                           &= 2 \times \dfrac {500} {5} \\\\
a                                                           &= \dfrac {2 \times 500} {5} \\\\
a                                                           &= \dfrac {2 \times 5 \times 100} {5} \\\\
a                                                           &= \dfrac {2 \times \cancel 5 \times 100} {\cancel 5} \\\\
a                                                           &= 2 \times 100 \\\\
a                                                           &= 200
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

</code></pre>

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Using equivalent ratio,

$
\begin{aligned}
3 : 1                                           &= 15 : a \\\\
3                                               &= \dfrac {15} {a} \\\\
a \times 3                                      &= 15 \\\\
a                                               &= \dfrac {15} {3} \\\\
a                                               &= \dfrac {5 \times 3} {3} \\\\
a                                               &= \dfrac {5 \times \cancel 3} {\cancel 3} \\\\
a                                               &= 5
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

What are the co-ordinates of the point $B$?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

                        &= \dfrac {12} {2} \\\\
                        &= 6
\end{aligned}
$

Coordinates $= (3, 6)$

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

**Estimate** the amount of Brie sold by Tosco in $1 \ \text{week}$.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">**Estimate** the amount of Brie sold by Tosco in $1 \ \text{week}$.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Brie sold by Tosco}               &= \dfrac {90} {360} \times 300 \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {90 \times 300} {360} \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {90 \times 4 \times 75} {90 \times 4} \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {\cancel {90} \times \cancel 4 \times 75} {\cancel {90} \times \cancel 4} \\\\
                                        &= 75 \ \text{kg}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Mean} = \dfrac {\text{Total of items}} {\text{Number of items}}$
</div>

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

\text{Average number of pizzas} &= \dfrac {15 + 13 + 8 + 10 + 5 + 9} {6} \\\\

                                &= \dfrac {10 \times 6} {6} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {10 \times \cancel 6} {\cancel 6} \\\\
                                &= 10
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

**Question**

What is the ratio of boys to girls in class $7B$? Give your answer in its simplest form.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">What is the ratio of boys to girls in class $7B$? Give your answer in its simplest form.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Ratio of boys to girls}       &= \dfrac {12} {8} \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {4 \times 3} {4 \times 2} \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {\cancel 4 \times 3} {\cancel 4 \times 2} \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {3} {2} \\\\
                                    &= 3 : 2
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

|     $2.5$    | $\dfrac{1} {3} \times 2.5 \times \sqrt{(90 - \pi 2.5^2) \times (90 + \pi 2.5^2)} = 73.19$ |
|     $3$      | $\dfrac{1} {3} \times 3 \times \sqrt{(90 - \pi 3^2) \times (90 + \pi 3^2)} = 85.44$       |
|     $3.5$    | $\dfrac{1} {3} \times 3.5 \times \sqrt{(90 - \pi 3.5^2) \times (90 + \pi 3.5^2)} = 94.92$ |
|     $4$      | $\dfrac{1} {3} \times 4 \times \sqrt{(90 - \pi 4^2) \times (90 + \pi 4^2)} = 99.54$       |
|     $4.5$    | $\dfrac{1} {3} \times 4.5 \times \sqrt{(90 - \pi 4.5^2) \times (90 + \pi 4.5^2)} = 95.49$ |
|     $5$      | $\dfrac{1} {3} \times 5 \times \sqrt{(90 - \pi 5^2) \times (90 + \pi 5^2)} = 73.25$       |

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Find the value of $x$ (other than $x = 0$) for which $y = 0$.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Find the value of $x$ (other than $x = 0$) for which $y = 0$.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
y               &= \dfrac {1} {3} \times x \times \sqrt{(90 - \pi x^2) \times (90 + \pi x^2)} \\\\
0               &= \dfrac {1} {3} \times x \times \sqrt{(90 - \pi x^2) \times (90 + \pi x^2)} \\\\
0 \times 3      &= x \times \sqrt{(90 - \pi x^2) \times (90 + \pi x^2)} \\\\
0               &= x \times \sqrt{(90 - \pi x^2) \times (90 + \pi x^2)} \\\\
0               &= \sqrt{x^2} \times \sqrt{(90 - \pi x^2) \times (90 + \pi x^2)} \\\\
0               &= \sqrt{x^2 \times (90 - \pi x^2) \times (90 + \pi x^2)} \\\\
0 ^ 2           &= x^2 \times (90 - \pi x^2) \times (90 + \pi x^2) \\\\
0               &= x^2 \times (90 - \pi x^2) \times (90 + \pi x^2) \\\\
0               &= 90 - \pi x^2 \\\\
0 + \pi x^2     &= 90 \\\\
\pi x^2         &= 90 \\\\
x^2             &= \dfrac {90} {\pi} \\\\
x               &= \sqrt{\dfrac {90} {\pi}} \\\\
x               &\approx 5.35
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
